brief: The ultimate guide to your first hire — 6 lessons from 50 founder interviews.

slots.title: Hire for Trajectory
slots.body: The best founders don't hire for today's skills. They bet on steep learners who adapt faster than the company grows.
slots.calloutBody: Early-stage problems change weekly; adaptability beats narrow expertise.

slots.title: Define the Pain First
slots.body: Never write a job description before you feel the burn. Founders who wait until a role is painfully missing hire with clarity.
slots.calloutBody: If you can't describe the pain in one sentence, you aren't ready to hire.

slots.title: Avoid Mini-Me Hiring
slots.body: Your first hire shouldn't share your exact strengths. Complementary skills prevent blind spots and build a balanced founding team.
slots.calloutBody: Diverse skill sets cover more ground with fewer people.

slots.title: Values Beat Pedigree
slots.body: Prestigious logos don't predict startup success. Founders who screen for shared values see higher retention and faster trust.
slots.calloutBody: Interviewees from top brands often flounder in ambiguous early-stage chaos.

slots.title: Reference Like a Detective
slots.body: Skip the back-channel casual check. Great founders conduct structured reference calls that reveal how candidates actually behave under pressure.
slots.calloutBody: Past behavior is the only reliable predictor of future performance.

slots.title: Generalists Win Early
slots.body: Specialists are luxury items at seed stage. Your first employee must wear five hats without waiting for permission or a playbook.
slots.calloutBody: One flexible operator replaces three narrow experts in month one.

slots.body: Save this guide and share it with a founder planning their first hire this quarter.
